df.text: Show how much space is used and free on the mounted file systems – with human-readable sizes (G, M).
df.hint: `df` shows the file systems, the `-h` option makes the sizes readable: `df -h`.

lsblk-f.text: Show all disks and partitions together with the file systems' type, label and UUID.
lsblk-f.hint: `lsblk` shows the disks as a tree. With `-f` the file systems are included: `lsblk -f`.

fstab.text: Show the file `/etc/fstab`, which says what should be mounted when the computer starts.

uuid.text: Find out the UUID of the file system mounted on `/` – and only that one.
uuid.hint: `lsblk -f` shows that `/` is on `/dev/sda2`. Then ask `blkid /dev/sda2` – or let `findmnt -n -o UUID /` do it all at once.

montera.text: Create the mount point `/mnt/usb` and mount the USB stick (`/dev/sdb1`) there.
montera.hint: Both creating directories in `/mnt` and mounting require root: `sudo mkdir -p /mnt/usb` and then `sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/usb`.

fran-usb.text: Copy `{{report}}` from the USB stick to your home directory.
fran-usb.hint: The stick's files are now in `/mnt/usb`: `cp /mnt/usb/{{report}} ~`.

till-usb.text: Save a copy of `~/{{documents}}/{{fruits}}` on the USB stick.
till-usb.hint: The files on the stick are owned by root – FAT has no Linux permissions – so you need `sudo`: `sudo cp ~/{{documents}}/{{fruits}} /mnt/usb/`.

avmontera.text: Unmount the USB stick, so that it is safe to pull out.
avmontera.hint: `sudo umount /mnt/usb` – without an n! If you get *target is busy*, your shell is in the directory: leave it with `cd ~` first.
